summary.text: Josh Turek is the Democratic nominee. A Council Bluffs native and four-time Paralympian on the U.S. wheelchair basketball team, he worked for a mobility-equipment company before winning a state House seat in 2022 by six votes. He is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst (R), emphasizing health care, public education and costs for middle-class families.

paragraphs.text: Born April 12, 1979, in Council Bluffs, Iowa; born with spina bifida, which he and his campaign link to his father's Agent Orange exposure in Vietnam, and underwent 21 surgeries by age 12.

Graduated from Abraham Lincoln High School in Council Bluffs, earned a bachelor's degree from Southwest Minnesota State University in 2002 (where he played wheelchair basketball), and later earned an MBA from DeVry University.

Played wheelchair basketball professionally in Europe for nearly two decades and on the U.S. national team in four Paralympic Games, winning a bronze medal (2012) and gold medals (2016, 2020), according to Wikipedia; his campaign website describes him as a two-time Paralympic gold medalist.

Worked at a wheelchair and mobility-equipment company (NuMotion, per Wikipedia), helping patients obtain mobility devices, and served as volunteer director of the Ryan Martin Foundation, which provides sports opportunities for children with disabilities, according to his campaign website.

Elected to Iowa House District 20 in 2022, winning by six votes out of about 6,800 cast after a recount requested by his opponent in a district that voted Republican in every presidential election since 1968; he took office January 9, 2023, as the legislature's first permanently disabled member, according to Wikipedia.

Re-elected in 2024 with 52.5% of the vote; serves on the House Health and Human Services Committee and the Health Policy Oversight Committee, and led bipartisan legislation (the "Work without Worry" program) removing Medicaid income limits for employed Iowans with disabilities, according to Wikipedia.
Announced his U.S. Senate candidacy on August 12, 2025, and won the Democratic primary over state Sen. Zach Wahls.

Has been inducted into the Athletic Halls of Fame at Abraham Lincoln High School and Southwest Minnesota State University and the National Wheelchair Basketball Association Hall of Fame; lives in Council Bluffs with his wife, Jarolin, who works in health care, according to his campaign website.
